title: The Joint Effect of Mother and Child's Functional Difficulties on Caregiver‐Reported Signs of Anxiety and Depression Among Children
abstract: ABSTRACT Childhood mental health disorders represent a significant public health challenge in low‐ and middle‐income countries, where resources for diagnosis and support are often limited. While functional difficulties are known to affect mental well‐being, the combined impact of maternal and child limitations within the household remains poorly understood. This study investigates the association between joint functional difficulties in mothers and children and caregiver‐reported signs of depression and anxiety among children in Bangladesh. Using data from the nationally representative 2019 Multiple Indicator Cluster Survey (MICS), we analyzed 44,898 children aged 5–14 years through division‐level prevalence mapping, logistic regression and classification tree models. Findings revealed substantial division‐level geographic variation in signs of depression (0.9%–33.4%) and anxiety (0.6%–16.2%) across the administrative divisions of Bangladesh. Children with functional difficulties whose mothers also experienced functional difficulties had significantly higher odds of showing signs of depression (AOR = 10.2 [95% CI: 6.91, 14.9]) and anxiety (AOR = 9.44 [6.51, 13.7]) compared to child–mother pairs without such difficulties. Classification tree analysis confirmed that regional variation and joint exposure were the most important predictors. Our findings suggest that both child and maternal functional limitations are strongly associated with child mental health, emphasising the need for targeted, region‐specific strategies that support the United Nations Sustainable Development Goals, particularly SDG Target 3.4 on promoting mental health and well‐being.
